local.h: Los Angeles details, verified against LA Superior Court
bullets: Your ticket is handled by the Superior Court of California, County of Los Angeles - Traffic Division. Start from the court's own traffic page - How do I pay my ticket? - which is the hub for payment, extensions, traffic school and court dates. There is no other official payment site for LA County tickets.

Pay online by looking the ticket up either by driver's license number or by citation number (both search boxes are on that page). You can also pay by phone, by mail, or in person at the courthouse printed on your ticket.

What paying really does: the court's page is blunt - the bail is declared forfeited, the case may be closed, and the ticket information is forwarded to the DMV and recorded on your driving record. Paying is not a way to keep a moving violation off your record.

Some tickets cannot be paid online or by phone at all. The court warns that certain violations require a mandatory court appearance, so check the violation code on your citation before assuming you can settle it online.

At an arraignment hearing you can do all four things in one visit: pay the bail, request traffic school if you are eligible, enter a plea of guilty / no contest / not guilty, or set the case for trial.

Traffic school is requested through the court itself - look for “How do I request traffic school?” and “How do I request a traffic school extension?” in the Q&A list on that same traffic page. California generally allows it once every 18 months on an eligible violation - see the state's traffic school rules.
Contest it without taking a day off: a trial by written declaration lets you argue your case in writing. The court's Trial Types section covers what it is and who qualifies.

Can't afford the full fine? LA runs its own Traffic Payment Plan (what it is, who qualifies and where to sign up are all in the Q&A list on the court's traffic page), and the statewide Ability to Pay portal is also open to you.
Parking tickets are not this court's business. They belong to the city or agency that issued them, so pay or contest through them, not the Superior Court.

local.h: San Diego details, verified against San Diego Superior Court
bullets: Your ticket is handled by the Superior Court of California, County of San Diego - Traffic / Minor Offense Division. Its jurisdiction covers Vehicle Code violations, some local municipal ordinances and infractions, and also Fish and Game, Animal Control and transit tickets such as San Diego Trolley violations.

Pay online at the court's own payment page: choose Traffic or Minor Offense Ticket, then Pay Now. New card fee: from 1 July 2026 the court's payment processing vendor may add a 2.75% service fee on credit, debit or prepaid card and mobile-wallet payments (Apple Pay, Google Wallet) - budget for it.

Scam alert, from the court itself: people are receiving text messages saying court fees on traffic tickets are overdue and action will be taken. The court does not conduct business by text message - official correspondence comes by U.S. mail. Check the court's online Traffic Portal for the real status of your ticket and ignore those texts.
Need to move your date? Traffic appearances are scheduled through Schedule Traffic Appearances.
Traffic school and pleading not guilty each have their own section in this division's menu on the court's traffic page - that is where the court's own instructions live.

Can't pay in full or on time? The division has a Payment Options and Financial Hardship Information section, and a dedicated Failure to Appear, Pay, or Comply page. Read that one before simply letting a deadline pass.

You may receive a reminder notice in the mail - for many drivers that is the first contact with the traffic court process, and the notice answers most of the usual questions. If it never arrives, the court's site explains what to do.

local.h: San Jose details, verified against Santa Clara County Superior Court
bullets: San Jose / Santa Clara County citations go to the Superior Court of California, County of Santa Clara, Traffic Division - it handles traffic and minor offences filed by law enforcement agencies inside the county.

Be patient, then don't be late. The court says a citation is usually entered in the system 4 to 8 weeks after you get it, and a Courtesy Notice comes 45 to 60 days after the citation with your options and a due date. You cannot pay or deal with the citation until it is in the system - check the Traffic Case Info Portal. If the notice has not arrived by the date printed at the bottom of your citation, you must contact the court by phone or in person.

How to pay: in person at any court location - cash, or a cheque payable to ‘Clerk/Superior Court’, or a card through NCourt (a 3.5% convenience fee, Amex, Discover, Mastercard, Visa); by mail with a cheque only (never send cash); or, for traffic cases that are eligible, by phone on 408-878-0098 (Mon–Fri 6pm–9pm, Sat–Sun 6am–3pm, Spanish available) or online at the Traffic Portal - card payments carry a 5% fee and an electronic fund transfer costs $1.95.

Fix-it tickets: your courtesy notice says whether you can just pay or must show proof of correction. Get the citation signed off by a police officer for equipment, the DMV for licence and registration, or a court clerk for insurance, licence and registration (bring the right documents). The police agency charges a fee to sign off and the court charges a dismissal fee - and any bail on a moving violation is payable on top. Then send the signed-off citation with the dismissal fee to the clerk.

Correcting a registration violation: show a valid registration card (valid now, or valid on the date of the violation), or get the DMV or a police officer to sign off, or show an official receipt from an identified junk dealer proving the vehicle was scrapped. The court does not accept a DMV ‘Suspense Receipt’ or a ‘Certificate of Non-operation’.

If you cannot fix the violation you can ask for a court date instead. If the violation does not require proof of correction, you can forfeit bail (pay) and close the case. If the ticket is not your vehicle but you signed the citation, you are still the responsible party - either forfeit bail or ask the clerk for a court date to explain to the commissioner.
If money is the problem, California also runs the statewide MyCitations portal for ability-to-pay requests.

local.h: San Francisco details, verified against the SF Superior Court - Traffic Division
bullets: Your ticket is handled by the Superior Court of California, County of San Francisco — Traffic Court. It hears infractions only (speeding, cell phone, expired registration, equipment): the worst outcome is a fine, never jail. Parking tickets are not handled here - those go to SFMTA, not the court.

A scam warning straight from the court: it never sends ticket notices by text message. If you get a text about a ticket, do not reply, click the link or scan the QR code - only the court's official phone numbers and website are real.

You should receive a Reminder Notice at the address on the citation, usually within 21 days of the ticket being issued. It shows the bail amount and due date, the proof required for correctable violations, and your court and traffic-school options. If it never arrives - still with the officer, DMV address not updated, wrong address on the ticket, returned by the post office - you are still expected to answer on time. Signing the citation was already your written promise to appear.

Miss the court date or the payment deadline and the court adds a $100 civil assessment, notifies the DMV (a possible point on your record), and hands the unpaid debt to the Alliance One collection agency, where wage garnishment and property liens are possible. The civil assessment can stand even if you later win the case.

Pay by phone (415) 551-8550, Mon–Fri 4am–9pm and Sat–Sun 9am–6pm PT; online through the court's nCourt portal (Visa, Amex, Mastercard, Discover, e-check); by mail (personal check or money order only); or in person (cash, cards, Apple Pay, check, money order). Online payment needs your case number and the amount due. Window service is at Hall of Justice, 850 Bryant St., Room 145 (8:30am–4pm, closed 12–1pm), and Civic Center Courthouse, 400 McAllister St., Room 103 - the Traffic Court itself sits in Department 218, 2nd floor.
The online payment page only takes money - it does not show case status or your court date. To check where your case stands or when you must appear, call 415-551-8540 or use the court's LiveChat.

Traffic school (Veh. Code 42005 + Cal. Rules of Court 4.104) needs a valid California licence, an eligible infraction, no more than one DMV point from this ticket, no traffic school in the last 18 months, no alcohol- or drug-related offence, speeding no more than 25 mph over the limit, and not the tanker-truck offence in VC 22406.5.

Correctable tickets (expired registration, no proof of insurance, equipment) are dismissed by showing proof - for insurance you must prove you were insured on the day of the ticket - plus a $25 fee per item. Mechanical defects need a police officer's signature before you send them in.

Lost at trial? You have 30 days to appeal - collect the 'Instructions on Appeal Procedures for Infractions' form at Hall of Justice Room 101, and keep paying the fine on time while you appeal. If you cannot afford to pay, ask for a determination of ability to pay before the due date: the court can cut the fine by 50–80% or more.

local.h: Sacramento details, verified against Sacramento County Superior Court
bullets: Sacramento County citations go to the Superior Court of California, County of Sacramento, Traffic Division. The traffic court is at the Carol Miller Justice Center, 301 Bicentennial Circle, Room 100, Sacramento, CA 95826. The call centre is 916-875-7800; extra options are available on 916-669-5712, through the Virtual Public Counter (Zoom) or in person.

The court's Public Case Access System is the online route to pay in full and close your case, request Traffic Violator School (or pay for it), request a monthly payment plan, and view or print case documents.

Paying in full - or setting up monthly payments - is a ‘bail forfeiture’: a conviction is reported to the DMV, your right to contest the ticket is gone, and once you sign up for monthly payments the case is no longer eligible for traffic school. Decide before you pay.

Ways to pay: online through the Public Case Access System with a credit or debit card; by phone on 916-875-7800; over Zoom at the Virtual Public Counter; in person at the Traffic Public Counter; or by mail or drop box with a cheque or money order payable to the Sacramento Superior Court. Note: postmarks are not accepted - the payment has to arrive by the due date.

Monthly payment plans need 10% of the full amount as a down payment; after that the Department of Revenue Recovery handles the monthly billing. Falling behind is expensive: collection enforcement can include garnishment of your wages, seizure of money in your bank accounts, a lien on real property, your balance reported to credit bureaus as delinquent, and seizure of your California state income tax refund.

Can't afford it? Two routes: the Alternative Sentencing Program - community service hours instead of all or part of the fine (you may still owe court fees plus application and daily fees to the Sacramento Sheriff's Department, scaled to your ability to pay) - or an Ability to Pay application, online through the MyCitations portal or on paper to the Traffic Division at the Carol Miller Justice Center. Applications are reviewed within 30 days. Watch the trap: on a case in active or failure-to-appear status the ability-to-pay form requires you to plead guilty or no contest, and once the court accepts that plea you can no longer appear in court. If you have been approved for Traffic Violator School, submit the ability-to-pay application at least 10 calendar days before the due date.
Trials can be held in person or over Zoom (Penal Code 1428.5) - tell the court at your next hearing if you do not consent to a remote trial.

local.h: Fresno details, verified against Fresno County Superior Court
bullets: Fresno County citations go to the Superior Court of California, County of Fresno, Traffic Division. The traffic court is at 2317 Tuolumne Street, Fresno, CA 93721 (clerk's office Mon–Fri 8am–4pm). You can also pay or write by mail to 1100 Van Ness Avenue, ATTN: Traffic Division, Fresno, CA 93724, by fax on (559) 457-1710, by email to InfoDeskCrim@fresno.courts.ca.gov, or via the drop box inside the M Street Courthouse. The call centre is (559) 457-1700, Mon–Fri 8am–4pm.

You must pay the bail on your reminder notice or appear on or before the due date - that date is printed at the bottom of your citation and on the reminder notice. To appear without an appointment you put yourself on the morning arraignment calendar (heard Monday to Wednesday) and must check in at the Traffic Clerk's Office by 9:30am; the lines are long, so arrive early.
Missing the deadline has a specific consequence: under California Vehicle Code 40903 the court may deem you to have elected a trial by written declaration.

Extensions: the clerk may grant one 90-day extension to appear or pay bail, but only on eligible citations that do not require a mandatory court appearance - and no further extensions are given after that 90 days. Ask online through the court's ePayIt system, by phone, by mail, or in person.

Delinquent fines are collected by an outside firm. If you get a letter from Linebarger (LGBS), pay at lgbswebpayments.com using the reference number on their letter, call 1-844-566-6558, or write to LGBS LLP, PO Box 708900, San Antonio, TX 78270.

Two things the online payment service cannot do: if you are pleading not guilty you may not use it - you must mail your written request for a court trial, with bail, to the court listed at the bottom of your citation; and you may not use it for fix-it violations, because the amount owing drops once you show proof of correction.

Fraud advisory from the court itself: scam text messages pretending to come from the California Judicial Branch, with links to fraudulent payment websites, are circulating. The Judicial Branch does not send unsolicited text messages about filed cases. Report a suspicious message to JCCInfoSec@jud.ca.gov.

local.h: Long Beach details, verified against LA Superior Court
bullets: Citations issued in Long Beach go to the Superior Court of California, County of Los Angeles, Traffic Division - and specifically to the courthouse printed on your citation. For Long Beach that is the Governor George Deukmejian Courthouse, 275 Magnolia Avenue, Long Beach, CA 90802 (LA Superior Court's South District, which also covers Signal Hill, San Pedro, Wilmington, Harbor City and Catalina). The court's own How do I pay my ticket? page is the only official place to pay, extend or set a court date for an LA County ticket.

Paying online: that page lets you find your ticket by driver's licence number or by citation number. You can also pay by phone, by mail, or in person at the courthouse on your ticket - the court lists the payment phone number next to each courthouse entry, so take it from the entry for the Long Beach courthouse.

What paying really means: the court's own wording is blunt - the bail is declared forfeited, the case may be closed, and the ticket information is forwarded to the DMV and recorded on your driving record. Paying is not a way to keep a moving violation off your record.

Some tickets cannot be paid online or by phone at all. The court warns that certain violations require a mandatory court appearance, so check the violation code on your citation before assuming you can settle it from your sofa.

At an arraignment you can do all four things in one visit: pay the bail, request traffic school if you are eligible, enter a plea of guilty, no contest or not guilty, or set the case for trial. If you would rather not go in, a trial by written declaration lets you argue the case in writing.

Cannot afford it? LA runs its own Traffic Payment Plan on the same page (who qualifies and how to sign up are in its Q&A list), and the statewide MyCitations ability-to-pay portal is open to LA County drivers too. California generally allows traffic school once every 18 months on an eligible violation - see the state's traffic school rules.

Questions: FM-ParkingCitation@longbeach.gov or (562) 570-6822. The city also offers standard and indigent payment plans for parking fines, and parking enforcement can be reached on (562) 570-2866.

local.h: Oakland details, verified against Alameda County Superior Court
bullets: Alameda County citations go to the Superior Court of California, County of Alameda, Traffic Division. Its three traffic courthouses are Fremont, Oakland (Wiley W. Manuel Courthouse) and Dublin (East County Hall of Justice) - the citation names the one that has your case.

The court's online system (alameda.epay-it.com) lets you: forfeit bail or pay a fine/fee, post bail for a court trial, post bail and request a trial by declaration, pay traffic school fees (bail plus enrolment fee), make a payment on an existing payment plan, extend your citation due date, fine due date or traffic-school completion date, confirm the court received your traffic-school certificate, and look up your ticket or print your courtesy notice.

Traffic school eligibility - you must meet all of it: pay the bail amount and the state-mandated traffic-school administrative fee before enrolling (on top of whatever the school charges); hold a valid licence at the time you were cited (since 13 Sep 2012 CDL holders driving a non-commercial vehicle are eligible); not have attended traffic school in the last 18 months (Veh. Code 1808.7 keeps only one citation per 18 months confidential, counted from violation date to violation date, not the class date); the citation must be a moving violation, not a misdemeanour, and you must not have been driving a commercial vehicle; the violation must not require a mandatory court appearance; nothing involving alcohol or drugs; not Veh. Code 22406.5 or 21655.5; and 25 mph or more over the limit is not eligible. Any failure to appear, warrant or civil assessment must be cleared or paid in full first.

Finish the course and file the certificate in time and, under Veh. Code 42007, the DMV keeps the conviction confidential - it will not show on your driving record. If you are eligible and skip traffic school, your auto insurance can be affected (Veh. Code 42007(f)).
Can't afford the fine? You can ask the court to lower it, set up a payment plan, give you more time, or do community service instead - see the court's financial hardship and ability-to-pay page.

Delinquent fines are referred to the court's collection agency, and the court's online payment tool does not work for delinquent fines: pay on the collection agency's website or call them on (844) 544-5358.
Scam alert posted by the court: scammers are impersonating the court's Pretrial Services to collect payment for GPS monitoring. The court does not collect money that way.

local.h: Anaheim details, verified against Orange County Superior Court
bullets: Citations issued in Anaheim are handled by the Superior Court of California, County of Orange, Traffic Division. The court's own city list puts Anaheim at the North Justice Center - 1275 North Berkeley Avenue, Fullerton, CA 92832, traffic counter (657) 622-8459 (Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.). Your citation still names the courthouse that has your case, so check the notice before you drive out.

You can extend the date twice before it turns into a failure to appear. The clerk can grant one 45-day extension and then one further 30-day extension before any failure-to-appear action (warrant, DMV hold or civil assessment) - this applies to mandatory and forfeitable infractions; anything beyond that must be referred to a judge. After you have paid the traffic school fine and fees you get one 30-day extension to finish the school, and one 30-day extension on a payment plan set up under Vehicle Code 40510.5 (not on traffic school plans). Request them in person at any Justice Center or online through My Court Portal.

How to pay: online through My Court Portal - you need your OC Pay # (printed on the citation - look it up here); internet payments only work on or before the original due date, and you cannot post bail online for a court trial or a trial by written declaration. By phone through the automated payment system. By mail: cheques or money orders only, never cash, payable to Clerk of the Court, preprinted with the maker's name and with the case or citation number on it, to Information Payment Center, P.O. Box 6040, Newport Beach, CA 92658-6040 (collected 24 hours a day). In person at any of the four Criminal & Traffic departments - Central (700 Civic Center Dr W, Santa Ana), Harbor (4601 Jamboree Rd, Newport Beach), North (1275 N Berkeley Ave, Fullerton) or West (8141 13th St, Westminster). Cash is accepted only in person; cards accepted are Visa, Mastercard, Discover and Diners Club.

Traffic school costs $54 to the court (the state fee) plus whatever the school itself charges. The clerk can authorise an 8-hour traffic violator school if you are a licensed driver and the offence is an infraction under the Vehicle Code rules of the road, or an equipment violation, that is reportable to the DMV. You are not eligible if the violation carries more than one point on your DMV record, if you elected traffic school within the last 18 months, if it is alcohol or drug related, if you failed to appear and an unpaid civil assessment was added, if the speeding was more than 25 mph over the limit, or if it happened in a commercial vehicle. Commercial-licence holders cited in a non-commercial vehicle may attend, but the conviction is not masked - no points are added instead.

Cannot afford the full amount? Ask for an Ability to Pay determination - a lower fine, a payment plan, community service or more time to pay. Requests go in through the statewide MyCitations tool or in person at any Justice Center (Central, Harbor, North or West). Be careful: if your case has not been decided yet, the court may require you to plead guilty or nolo contendere before it will consider your ability to pay.
Contesting it yourself: the court's Contesting Your Citation page sets out the options, including a trial by written declaration if you would rather not take a day off work.
Parking tickets are not this court's business. They are issued and handled by the City of Anaheim's parking enforcement, so pay or contest them through the city - not the Superior Court.

Deadline warning: missing the date on your citation can add a civil assessment and put a hold on your licence. The court's failure to appear page explains what happens next, and the current fines and bail schedule information is on the court's fines page.

bullets: City of Houston tickets go to the City of Houston Municipal Courts Department - that is the court this page covers. If the court printed on your citation is a Harris County Justice of the Peace court instead, pay through the county at jp.hctx.net.

Pay online through the city's ticket payment page - and read its warning: the payment is processed as two separate transactions, the fine first and the service fee second. On a debit or prepaid card, tell your bank two charges are coming and keep enough in the account: if the second one fails, the first is declined too and your bank may hold the money for up to 30 days.

You cannot pay a Driver Safety Course or a Deferred Disposition through the online payment link - those are requests, not payments. You must appear on or before your scheduled court date, or follow the mail / email instructions.

Driver Safety Course (DSC) - Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Art. 45A.354 lets you get a charge dismissed by successfully completing a driving safety course. You must ask on or before your arraignment date or you lose the right. You are not eligible if you have no valid Texas driver's license, you held a CDL when you were cited, you took a court-ordered DSC within one year of this citation, or you were charged with 95 mph or more, 25 mph or more over the posted limit, passing a school bus, a serious traffic violation, failing to stop and give information or render aid, or an offence in a construction zone with workers present. Juveniles must apply in person with a parent or guardian. Requirements and the application form

Deferred Disposition is a suspended sentence. You plead guilty or no contest, the court defers a finding of guilt and you post a bond and meet conditions: complete them and the case is dismissed (the bond is applied to a special expense fee), fail and it is a conviction reported to the Texas Department of Public Safety. Ask on or before your first court date, in person, by phone or by mail. On a moving violation, if you are under 25 the judge must require a driver safety course; CDL holders are not eligible. Some cases - 26 mph or more over the limit, CDL holders, passing a school bus, no liability insurance, construction-zone violations - must be requested in person. Full rules
Fixed the problem? Some tickets can be dismissed after the fact by proving compliance - the city's Post Compliance page says what qualifies and what proof to send.
Parking tickets are a separate system. Pay or contest a City of Houston parking citation from the parking citations page, not the traffic ticket link.
Contesting a ticket, changing your court date, fines and fees, and what happens if you neglect a ticket each have their own page - the department's Ticket Information hub links them all.

local.h: San Antonio details, verified against the San Antonio Municipal Court
bullets: City of San Antonio citations go to the San Antonio Municipal Court, 401 S. Frio St., San Antonio, TX 78207, 210-207-8970, open Monday to Friday 8am-4:30pm (closed on city holidays). If the citation names a Bexar County Justice of the Peace precinct instead, it is a county case - pay the county, not the city. The Magistrate Court and the Detention Center are open 24/7.
Pay or resolve online at the Municipal Court online payment portal, and look up a case or docket at municipalrecordsearch.com/sanantoniotx.

Driver Safety Course (defensive driving): plead no contest or guilty, pay the court costs, and complete a course approved by the Texas Department of Licensing & Regulation (TDLR) and the charge is dismissed. Not every violation qualifies. You need a valid Texas licence (a permit or active-military status also works), current liability insurance with your name on the policy (no commercial policies), no DSC in the last 12 months, no CDL, and you must not have been 25 mph or more over the limit, at 95 mph or more, passing a school bus loading or unloading children, in a construction or work zone with workers present, or leaving the scene of a collision. You also pay the state and administrative fees when you request - the court notes these change with state law.
Deferred Disposition is probation: you ask the judge to place you on deferred disposition, agree to the conditions, and the citation is dismissed when you complete them.
Compliance and dismissal: for certain violations you can have the ticket dismissed by showing proof that you fixed the defect.

Don't ignore an old ticket. In August 2025 the court contracted with the collection firm Linebarger Goggan Blair & Sampson LLP to chase delinquent criminal, parking and civil code citations. Under Texas law municipal citations do not expire - they stay enforceable until resolved. The court also warns that scam texts impersonating government and collection agents are going around: a genuine Linebarger text only ever comes from the short code 98023.

Once you appear, the court says a judge can reduce or waive amounts due, grant extensions, order community service, or authorise other alternatives to payment. Notices on unadjudicated cases still give you the chance to contest the case and set it for trial.

local.h: Dallas details, verified against the Dallas Municipal Court
bullets: City of Dallas citations go to the Dallas Municipal Court (Court & Detention Services), 2014 Main St., Dallas, TX 75201, 214-670-0109. If the court printed on your citation is a Dallas County Justice of the Peace instead, that is a county court - pay there, not the city. Parking citations are separate: pay or appeal them at cityofdallas.rmcpay.com. Look up any citation - warrants show in red - at Dallas Citation Search.

Watch the 21-day clock. The court warns that for a driving safety course “once you are past the 21 days, the amount may be higher, or this option may no longer be available”. After 21 days from the file date your options are listed on the court's ‘citations over 21 days’ page.

What paying means. Paying online enters a plea of No Contest or Guilty, waives your right to a jury trial and to discovery, and a finding of guilt may be reported to the Texas Department of Public Safety (Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 27.14(c)). Payments made after hours, at weekends or on holidays do not post until the next business day. Online runs 24/7, Visa or Mastercard only, with a convenience fee.

Other ways to pay: by phone through AllPaid on 1-833-256-5997 (24/7, Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover); cash at a retail store - nearly 27,000 locations including 7-Eleven, CVS, RiteAid and Walmart, but you must call AllPaid first to get the barcode you need; by mail - a check, cashier's check or money order payable to ‘City of Dallas’ with the citation number printed on it (the postmark is the received date, certified mail is recommended but not required, and never send cash); or in person with cash, debit or credit card, check or money order. Paying cash or by cheque avoids the card convenience fee.

Driving Safety Course (DSC): you need a valid Texas licence (other states' licences are not accepted), an insurance policy naming you as a driver, no DSC in the previous 12 months, no CDL (even when you were driving your own car), and you must not have been 25 mph or more over the limit, at 95 mph or more, passing a school bus, in a construction or maintenance zone with workers present, leaving the scene of a collision, or charged with a serious traffic violation. The fee is $144 outside a school zone and $169 inside one. Requesting online or by mail is a request only - the court replies by mail in 5-7 business days and you must not start the class before you are approved. You then have 90 days, with no extensions, and also need the 3A version of your driving record plus a notarised affidavit. National Safety Council and AARP courses are not approved.

Deferred Disposition keeps the citation off your driving record - the judge dismisses it when you complete the terms. Not available to CDL holders or for construction-zone offences with workers present. If you are under 25 and charged with a moving violation the court must require a driving safety course as a term; a provisional-licence holder must be examined by DPS ($10 fee); an under-21 alcohol offence requires an alcohol-awareness course, and certain minor alcohol or tobacco offences require community service. Some cases must be approved by a judge: 25 mph or more over the limit, any juvenile case (you appear with a parent or guardian), Class C assault, theft or reckless damage, minor alcohol or tobacco charges, and public intoxication under 21. You need acceptable photo ID (a Social Security card or a selfie is not accepted) and payment in full.

Already past 21 days? Your options are: pay in full; set up a payment plan; pay in full for deferred disposition; plead not guilty and post a cash bond equal to the citation amount to get a court date; file a motion by mail or in person only (phone, email, fax and live chat are not accepted); walk-in Proof or Plea court; a compliance dismissal by showing a valid licence or proof of insurance; community service; or time served. A past-due request is answered by mail in 3-4 weeks.

Civil (code / ordinance) citations are a separate system with an administrative hearing officer at 2014 Main St.: you must answer by the 31st calendar day after the citation was issued, a corporation must be represented by an attorney, hearings are first-come first-served from 7:30am, and violations can carry civil penalties of up to $1,000 a day. The court also posts a warning about text alerts sent by its collections firm, Linebarger Goggan Blair & Sampson.

local.h: Austin details, verified against the Austin Municipal Court
bullets: Austin citations go to the Austin Municipal Court, the City of Austin's court for Class C misdemeanours - traffic, city ordinance, juvenile and disabled-parking cases. Main courthouse: 6800 Burleson Road, Building 310, Suite 175, Austin, TX 78744; phone 512-974-4800. Hours are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 8am-6pm and Thursday 8am-8pm. There is a second walk-in location, the North Customer Service Center, 2121 West Parmer Lane, Suite 116, Austin, TX 78727 (Mon-Fri 8am-4:30pm).

Two steps: look up your case (you need your last name and date of birth, or your driver's licence number) and then choose how to resolve it. The city's Handle a citation page walks through every option.

Paying means pleading. To pay fines, fees and court costs you must first enter a plea of guilty or nolo contendere (no contest) - a no-contest plea means you are not admitting guilt but are not contesting the violation either. You can pay four ways: online through the case portal; on the payment line 512-974-4800 (Mon-Fri 8am-5pm, excluding holidays); by mail to Austin Municipal Court, P.O. Box 2135, Austin, TX 78768-2135, with the licence plate number, date of violation, citation number and your contact details, cheques payable to ‘Austin Municipal Court’; or in person at either courthouse (Western Union is also accepted). If you cannot pay, ask the court about alternative payment options.

Deferral is a postponement of judgment: asking for one includes a no-contest or guilty plea, and it gives you a window to remedy or offset the violation - for example by getting and keeping insurance, or by taking a driver safety course - while you pay the associated court fees and avoid committing the same type of violation. Complete the terms and the case is dismissed. The cost varies and shows in the online portal once your request is processed.

Compliance dismissal: fix the problem, then ask the court online or in person to dismiss the case. It sometimes carries a fee of up to $20. It covers common charges such as no driver's licence, failure to display a licence, expired licence, no motorcycle licence, no child safety seat, no insurance, expired registration, unregistered vehicle, unregistered out-of-state vehicle and licence plates; defective-equipment charges may also qualify. If your charge is not listed, contact the court to ask whether it is eligible.
Disabled parking citations have their own online form - use it to show you were not responsible for the vehicle at the time, or that you did have a placard.

Want a hearing instead? Email the court to ask for an appearance docket (to discuss the case with a prosecutor before trial), use the online form for a trial by judge, or email the court for a trial by jury. Note that from 5 October 2026 all attorney appearance dockets and jury trials at the Austin Municipal Court are held only on Tuesdays. Walk-in mitigation runs in person on Thursday evenings, 6pm-8pm, to discuss warrants, commitments and pending cases with a judge.

Scam alert - ‘vishing’: the court warns of fake phone calls from people posing as officers or jury officials. Court business is never conducted by cold call - hang up and call 512-974-4800 yourself. Also note that delinquent cases can be sent to a collection agency, and unpaid cases can stop a juvenile or minor from renewing a driver's licence.

bullets: A city citation goes to the Corpus Christi Municipal Court, 120 N. Chaparral Street, Corpus Christi, TX 78401 - 361-826-2500, MCMail@CorpusChristiTX.gov. Open 8am-4pm Monday to Friday, with extended hours Thursdays until 6pm; the site has a free parking map.

Pay online at the city's payment portal. Search with your citation number in the format CT012345 (capitals) plus your date of birth as MM/DD/YYYY. The portal adds a 3% credit-card fee plus a $2.50 online convenience fee, charged separately.

Trap - paying is pleading. The portal states that if you pay a new citation without a court order, a plea of no contest and a judgment are entered, and the conviction is reported to the Texas Department of Public Safety for your driving record. Only pay in full if you mean to accept the conviction.

All the options in one place: the court's citation options hub links pay online, request deferred disposition, request defensive driving, pay by phone (1-866-299-7084), pay by mail or in person, payment plans (MCPaymentPlan@CorpusChristiTX.gov) and time served.

Driving safety course. You must elect it on or before the appearance date on the citation and plead no contest or guilty, sign an affidavit under penalty of perjury, and then complete everything in the DSC order within 90 days. You are not eligible if you hold a CDL (or held one at the time of the offence), were charged with 25 mph or more over the limit or 95 mph or more, were charged with a city ordinance violation and you are 25 or older, were in a construction or maintenance zone with workers present, passed a school bus, or failed to give information and render aid - and you must not have taken a DSC for a dismissal in the 12 months before this citation.

County citations: citations filed by Nueces County deputies or constables go to a Nueces County Justice of the Peace, not this court - see the Nueces County JP courts (for example JP 1-1 at 901 Leopard St., Room 116, 361-888-0201).
Need to move a court date? The court takes motions by email (MCMotions@CorpusChristiTX.gov) and publishes a motion for continuance form.

bullets: A city citation goes to the El Paso Municipal Court, 810 E. Overland Ave., El Paso, TX 79901 - 915-212-0215 (choose option 7 for a court representative). Court locations: Pebble Hills, Mission Valley and Northeast; the Westside location is closed.

Ways to pay: in person at any court location, by phone at 915-212-0232, by mail (cheque, money order or cashier's cheque payable to City of El Paso, with your ticket number, driver's licence number and date of birth written on it - cheques are converted to electronic transfers), or online by card. Cash, personal/cashier's cheques, money orders, cards and Apple/Samsung Pay are accepted.

Trap - someone else cannot pay it for you. The court states a citation may not be paid by another person unless the case has a guilty disposition or a payment plan, and the person cited must be present with ID to pay in person. Also, warrants stay active until the ticket is paid in full.

Fines and costs: most municipal traffic violations top out at a $200 fine, penal violations at $500, and city ordinance violations at $500-$2,000. The fine is set on the facts of the case, and state-mandated court costs are added - a jury trial adds $3, and if a peace officer served the warrant another $50 is assessed.

Paying over time costs more. State law makes the court add a reimbursement fee to each violation on the 31st day from the date of conviction if the fine is not paid in full - so pay inside the first 30 days and it does not apply.

Parking is a separate system handled off the same court page: $25-$275 depending on the violation, $10 more for each 30 days delinquent (capped at $60), plus a 30% collection-agency fee applied on the 75th day after the ticket was issued. You can request an in-person parking hearing within 14 days of the citation.

Driving safety course by right: request it at your scheduled court hearing, online, by mail to 810 E Overland, El Paso, TX 79901, or in person - then finish within 90 days and file your 3A certified driving record from DPS, the TDLR court-copy certificate of completion and proof of insurance. You are not eligible without a valid Texas licence (or active military / military family with a valid licence), with a CDL, if you took a DSC for a traffic offence in the last 12 months, if you were 25 mph or more over the limit, or on the listed offences such as failure to give information at an accident scene.
Under 17? State law requires you to appear before a judge with a parent or legal guardian before paying - fines mailed in before that appearance are not accepted.

City or county? If a city officer wrote the ticket it is a city case. El Paso County's seven Justice of the Peace precincts handle county-filed cases - the county JP directory lists every precinct's address, phone and hours (Precinct 1, for example, is at 424 Executive Center, Suite 100, 915-273-3052).

To clear a warrant you can pay the full warrant amount by phone at 602-262-6421 (partial payments are not accepted), and payment in full is also available 24 hours a day at the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office, 201 S. 4th Ave.

Defensive driving instead of paying: if your violation is a civil traffic violation you can elect a defensive driving class at an Arizona Supreme Court certified school. The school reports your completion and the charge is dismissed from your record. If you live out of state you must take an online course or come back to Arizona for a classroom course. Need the date moved? The court requires a written continuance request within 7 days of your court date.

Do not rely on same-day updates. The court sends MVD updates daily, but MVD records can take up to 72 hours to catch up - so a warrant you just cleared can still show up on a police check for a few days.
To contest it, you enter a not-guilty plea and the court sets a hearing; the court's own self-service site is the place to check your case status and what you owe before you decide.

cities.pay_label: Las Vegas Justice Court - look up and pay a traffic citation
cities.court_label: Las Vegas Justice Court (Clark County) official site
cities.fine_note: Nevada now splits traffic citations into civil infractions and criminal traffic violations. The fine depends on the violation and is set by the court - the citation shows your response date.
cities.school_eligible: Nevada does not dismiss a ticket with a course, but the DMV gives a 3-point demerit reduction for a DMV-approved traffic safety course when you have 3-11 active points, generally once every 12 months. A course you take under a court plea agreement does not earn that reduction.
cities.points_note: Nevada counts demerit points: 12 or more in a 12-month period can suspend your licence.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical
cities.tool_note: Nevada has no ticket-dismissal course. The DMV course only knocks 3 points off an existing record once a year, and a court-ordered course does not count for it.

local.h: Las Vegas details, verified against Las Vegas Justice Court
bullets: Most traffic citations in the Las Vegas valley are filed with the Las Vegas Justice Court (Clark County), 1st floor, Regional Justice Center, 200 Lewis Ave. The court's own site is where you check whether your citation has been loaded yet - it is common for a citation not to appear for days after the stop, and the court's advice is to check back weekly rather than assume it is missing.

Two different lanes since Nevada's 2023 changes (Assembly Bill 116 of the 81st session): a civil infraction and a criminal traffic violation. A civil infraction gets a window measured from the date the citation is made available online. If there is a court date printed on your citation, it is a criminal traffic case and you must appear.

Paying: uncontested civil infractions can be paid online on the court's site. Contesting a civil infraction is in person only - you must go to the court's Customer Service Division on the 1st floor of the Regional Justice Center; there is no online contest for a civil infraction.
Regulatory criminal citations - licence, registration, insurance and handicap placard violations - can be handled online on the same court site.

Points: Nevada's DMV removes 3 demerit points for a DMV-approved traffic safety course if you have between 3 and 11 active points, generally once every 12 months (Nevada DMV points page). Twelve points in 12 months can suspend your licence, and at that level the voluntary reduction no longer helps.

Check the court name. Henderson and North Las Vegas have their own justice courts. If your citation names Henderson Justice Court, that court handles it - and it does not take payment by phone. Juveniles under 18 are not eligible for online payment anywhere and must appear with a parent or guardian.

cities.pay_label: Denver County Court - pay a ticket or fine online
cities.court_label: Denver County Court - official site
cities.fine_note: Denver County Court sets the fine on the facts of the case and adds costs. A photo radar or photo red-light notice carries a set penalty printed on the notice.
cities.school_eligible: Colorado does not remove points after a conviction, so there is no course that cleans the record. What exists is a deferral or plea agreement in the case itself, and at the DMV a point-suspension hearing where you can raise mitigating circumstances or ask for a probationary licence.
cities.points_note: Colorado suspends an adult driver at 12 points in 12 months; points stay on your record for two years from the offence.
cities.lawyer_cost: $300-$500 typical
cities.tool_note: Colorado cannot erase points after the fact. In Denver the realistic routes are posting bond and contesting the case, or dealing with the points at a DMV hearing later.

local.h: Denver details, verified against Denver County Court
bullets: Denver is a consolidated city and county, so city traffic tickets go to the Denver County Court, Traffic Division, 1437 Bannock Street, Room 140. Pay online through the court's public portal - but note the portal will not let you pay fines and costs while there is an outstanding warrant or bond on the case; you must post bond or address the warrant first.

Photo radar and photo red light notices are issued by the police department rather than at a traffic stop. You will need the notice number and city code. Pay online, or by mail - cheques, cashier's cheques or money orders payable to Manager of Finance - to Denver Photo Enforcement Program, Payment Center, PO Box 17909, Denver, CO 80217. There is also a drop box at the Traffic Division, 1437 Bannock St., Room 140: it is a payment drop box only, so a clerk there cannot take a payment from you.
The respond-by date is an arraignment date. On a penalty assessment notice, the respond-by/arraignment date is when you must act; missing it can add costs and eventually a warrant.

Points: Colorado suspends an adult driver at 12 points in 12 months, and points stay on your record two years. You can request a non-alcohol (points) hearing through myDMV to check that the points were calculated correctly, raise mitigating circumstances, or ask for a probationary licence that keeps you driving to work. A points hearing cannot revisit whether you were guilty - that happened in traffic court.
Check the court name. A ticket written by a state trooper outside Denver city limits belongs to a county court (Arapahoe, Jefferson, Adams and so on), not to Denver County Court.

cities.pay_label: Seattle Municipal Court - pay my ticket
cities.court_label: Seattle Municipal Court - dispute my ticket (hearings, deadlines, evidence)
cities.fine_note: Washington sets a statewide penalty schedule for civil traffic infractions, so the base fine for a given infraction is the same across the state; the amount is printed on the notice along with any local assessments.
cities.school_eligible: Washington has no traffic-school dismissal. The equivalent is a deferred finding: the court defers the ticket for up to a year and, if you stay violation-free through the deferral, it never goes on your record. Most drivers get one deferral for a moving and one for a non-moving infraction every seven years.
cities.points_note: Washington does not use points. A civil infraction still shows on your DOL record for three years and can affect your insurance - a deferred finding keeps it off, which is the real prize.
cities.lawyer_cost: $300-$500 typical
cities.tool_note: Washington's version of traffic school is a deferred finding (RCW 46.63.070) - ask the court to defer and stay clean for the deferral period.

local.h: Seattle details, verified against Seattle Municipal Court
bullets: A ticket from Seattle police goes to the Seattle Municipal Court. A Washington State Patrol ticket written on a highway is a King County District Court case instead - the court named on the notice is the one that matters.

Four ways to respond: pay the full amount, ask the court about a payment plan, ask for a mitigation hearing (you accept that you broke the rule but want to explain the circumstances), or ask for a contested hearing (you say you did not break the rule).
The deadline is the whole game: you must ask for a hearing within 30 days if the ticket was handed to you or placed on your car, or 33 days if it was mailed to you. Miss it and you lose the hearing.

How to ask: the online hearing request form is the easiest route; you can also check the box on the back of the ticket and bring or mail it to Seattle Municipal Court, PO Box 34987, Seattle, WA 98124-4987, or call (206) 684-5600. The court mails or emails your hearing date and time.

What happens at the hearing: a contested hearing starts with a pre-hearing settlement conference, a chance to resolve it without a full hearing - you can skip that and go straight to trial by returning the waiver form sent with your notice. Two traps: if you contest in writing you cannot appeal, and a mitigation decision is final too - so send your photos and documents in first (upload to the Public Portal or email CourtCalendar.SMC@seattle.gov).

The deferred finding is Washington's real record-protection tool: the court can defer the finding for up to a year and impose conditions; complete them and the infraction does not go on your record. Most drivers can use it once for a moving and once for a non-moving infraction every seven years.

cities.pay_label: Municipal Court of Atlanta - pay a ticket / look up your case (PTIT)
cities.court_label: Municipal Court of Atlanta - official court site
cities.fine_note: If your citation is eligible for online payment, the fine appears when you look your case up in the court's Find My Case tool. If it is not, only a judge sets the fine and you have to appear.
cities.school_eligible: Georgia has no course that dismisses a ticket. The record-protection tool is a nolo contendere plea: it is reported to DDS and shows on your record, but no points are assessed. You may only use it once every five years, and the judge decides whether to accept it.
cities.points_note: Georgia assesses 2-6 points per violation, and 15 points in 24 months suspends your licence - DDS publishes the exact point value for every offence code.
cities.lawyer_cost: $300-$600 typical
cities.tool_note: In Georgia the record-protection move is a nolo contendere plea - once every five years, at the judge's discretion - not a course.

local.h: Atlanta details, verified against the Municipal Court of Atlanta
bullets: A citation from an Atlanta police officer goes to the Municipal Court of Atlanta - the largest municipal court in Georgia, with jurisdiction over traffic offences inside the city limits, including DUI and city ordinance violations. It also handles the city's camera enforcement: photo school-bus violations, false alarms, parking and code enforcement. A ticket written in the county rather than the city goes to a Fulton County court.

Paying: if your citation is eligible for online payment, a green payment button appears when you view the case in the court's Find My Case tool, and you pay on the court's payment portal with a credit or debit card (American Express, Discover, Visa, Mastercard). The fine must be paid in full.

Timing tip: if you pay in full by the business day before your scheduled court date, you do not need to attend court. If your citation is not eligible for online payment, a judge determines the final fine at your appearance - some offences require a mandatory appearance.
Other payment routes: money orders by mail or in person; cash in person; Apple Pay and Tap-to-Pay in person, with a 3% convenience fee added to the fine.

A guilty plea is reported to the Georgia Department of Driver Services and points can be assessed against your licence. If you hold a commercial driver's licence, the court's own guidance is to contact DDS before paying online, because the consequences are different for CDL holders.
Cannot pay in full? You must appear before a judge to be considered for payment options and alternatives - there is no instalment button online.

cities.pay_label: Orange County Clerk of Courts - traffic tickets (pay, elect school, request a hearing)
cities.court_label: Orange County Clerk of Courts - traffic division
cities.fine_note: In Florida the fine for a traffic infraction comes from a statewide penalty schedule plus county surcharges, and the amount is printed on the citation. The county Clerk of Courts collects it - not a city court.
cities.school_eligible: Florida lets you elect a 4-hour Basic Driver Improvement course instead of paying points: the adjudication is withheld and no points are assessed. You generally have 30 days from the citation to make the election, and you can only do it once in a 12-month period.
cities.points_note: Florida adds 3, 4 or 6 points per moving violation and suspends at 12 points in 12 months, 18 in 18 months or 24 in 36 months. Points stay on your record three years.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical
cities.tool_note: In Florida the record-protection route is electing Basic Driver Improvement within about 30 days - do that before you simply pay, because paying closes the door.

local.h: Orlando details, verified against the Orange County Clerk of Courts
bullets: Florida has no city traffic court for this. The county Clerk of Courts collects traffic fines: for Orlando that is the Orange County Clerk of Courts, 425 N. Orange Ave., Orlando, FL 32801 - 407-836-2000 (Monday to Friday, 7:30am-4:00pm).

Ways to pay: online at MyOrangeClerk.com with your case or citation number; by mail (cheque or money order only, payable to Orange County Clerk of Courts, 425 N. Orange Ave., Orlando, FL 32801); by phone at 407-836-2000; in person; or in cash at Amscot and Western Union locations. Payments are not accepted at county Public Works offices.

Your four responses are all explained on the clerk's own notice: pay, elect a Basic Driver Improvement course, file an affidavit accepting or denying responsibility (downloadable from ViolationInfo.com - it must reach the clerk on or before the due date), or request a hearing by signing and mailing the original citation to the clerk. Failure to respond by the due date starts the penalty ladder.
Need more time? Request an extension online. Orange County charges $4 per 30-day extension and allows a maximum of two.

Electing the course is the record-protection move: a Basic Driver Improvement course is the difference between a withheld adjudication and a conviction with points. Do the election inside the window the citation gives you - and remember the clock runs from the citation date, not from when you got round to it.

Points: Florida's thresholds are 12 points in 12 months (30-day suspension), 18 in 18 months (three months) and 24 in 36 months (one year); points stay three years, and they are counted from the violation date, not the payment date.

cities.pay_label: Miami-Dade Clerk of Courts - traffic ticket payment app
cities.court_label: Miami-Dade Clerk of Courts - traffic/misdemeanor division
cities.fine_note: Florida's fine comes from the statewide penalty schedule plus county surcharges, printed on your citation. The Clerk of Courts collects it, not a city court.
cities.school_eligible: Florida lets you elect a 4-hour Basic Driver Improvement course to keep points off your record, generally within 30 days of the citation and once in a 12-month period. That election is the single biggest decision on a Miami moving violation.
cities.points_note: Florida adds 3, 4 or 6 points per moving violation and suspends at 12 points in 12 months, 18 in 18, or 24 in 36. Points stay on your record three years.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical
cities.tool_note: In Florida the record-protection route is electing Basic Driver Improvement inside the 30-day window - and check for an Operation Green Light amnesty event before paying off older tickets.

local.h: Miami details, verified against the Miami-Dade Clerk of Courts
bullets: Miami-Dade handles its own traffic citations: the Clerk of the Courts, Traffic/Misdemeanor Division. This covers citations on I-95, the Palmetto and local streets across Miami, Hialeah, Miami Gardens and the rest of the county.

Ways to pay: online through the clerk's traffic app; by mail - cheque or money order to Clerk of Courts, Traffic/Misdemeanor Division, P.O. Box 19321, Miami, FL 33101-9321; by the 24-hour automated phone system at (305) 275-1111; or in person at a district court office (Joseph Caleb Center, 5400 NW 22nd Ave., Suite 103; Coral Gables, 3100 Ponce de Leon Blvd; Hialeah, 11 E. 6th Street; and others).

Same Florida election rules as the rest of the state: pay, elect Basic Driver Improvement to avoid points, file an affidavit accepting or denying responsibility, or request a hearing. The deadline on the citation is real - miss it and penalty fees are added.

Check for amnesty before paying old tickets. The clerk runs Operation Green Light events where drivers with older unpaid tickets can pay the original fine and get collection fees waived and licence holds lifted. If you have a pile of old Miami tickets, look for the next event before you pay them off one by one.
Points and suspension follow Florida's statewide thresholds: 12 points in 12 months is a 30-day suspension, 18 in 18 months is three months, 24 in 36 months is a year.

cities.pay_label: Clerk of the Circuit Court of Cook County - pay traffic tickets online
cities.court_label: Circuit Court of Cook County - Traffic Section
cities.fine_note: Illinois sets fines by statute. For the violations that can be settled without a court appearance, the fine plus costs is listed on the back of the ticket. Chicago camera and parking tickets are city administrative tickets, not court tickets.
cities.school_eligible: Illinois uses court supervision rather than traffic school: if you are eligible, the case is diverted on conditions and, if you complete them, is dismissed without a conviction. A Traffic Safety School course is often one of the conditions - Cook County's school runs in class and online, in English, Spanish and Polish.
cities.points_note: Illinois reports convictions to the Secretary of State and adds points to your record; supervision means no conviction - which is the whole point of asking for it.
cities.lawyer_cost: $300-$600 typical
cities.tool_note: In Illinois the record-protection route is court supervision (often with Cook County's Traffic Safety School attached) - not simply paying.

local.h: Chicago details, verified against the Circuit Court of Cook County
bullets: All traffic offences in Chicago (other than parking) are heard in the Traffic Section of the Circuit Court of Cook County, part of the First Municipal District at the Richard J. Daley Center, 50 W. Washington St., Chicago, IL 60602 - Traffic Section phone (312) 603-2600, Clerk of the Circuit Court (312) 603-2000. Traffic offences written outside Chicago are heard in the municipal district where the violation happened.

Parking, red-light cameras and speed cameras are not court tickets. Those are city administrative tickets: you pay or contest them through the City of Chicago, not the court. Mixing these two systems up is the most common mistake drivers make here.

Mail-in settlement: for the violations Illinois classifies as fine-only, the back of the ticket gives you the options. Sign the guilty plea form, mark the PAYMENT ENCLOSED box, and mail a cheque or money order payable to Clerk of the Circuit Court with your ticket numbers written on it, within seven days. Do not send cash, and note Illinois law does not allow payment by credit card by mail. Your licence or bond card and a signed receipt come back - keep the receipt for two years.

Court supervision is the record-protection route. If you are eligible, asking for supervision (and completing any conditions, including Traffic Safety School where ordered) means no conviction on your record instead of a guilty plea. Cook County's Traffic Safety School offers classroom and online courses in English, Spanish and Polish.
Some offences can never be settled by mail or supervision - passing a school bus and illegally transporting alcohol are the ones the court names. Those need a court date.

The Illinois Supreme Court divides traffic offences into two categories: the ones that can be settled without appearing, and the ones that require an appearance. Reading the back of your ticket tells you which one you have before you do anything else.

cities.pay_label: MassDOT / RMV - pay your traffic ticket
cities.court_label: MassDOT / RMV - request a hearing on a traffic ticket
cities.fine_note: Massachusetts fines are set by statute and printed on the citation. Miss the 20-day window and the RMV adds late and release fees on top of the fine, then suspends your licence if you do not pay within 30 days of the default letter.
cities.school_eligible: Massachusetts has no course that dismisses a ticket. What protects you is winning or amending the citation at a hearing - insurance surcharges follow 'responsible' findings, not course credits. Only drivers with three surchargeable events in two years are required to complete the RMV's Driver Retraining Program.
cities.points_note: Massachusetts does not use points. Insurers assign SDIP surcharge points after a 'responsible' finding, which raises your premium for years - which is why the hearing matters more than the fine.
cities.lawyer_cost: $300-$600 typical
cities.tool_note: Massachusetts is not a traffic-school state: the RMV is the decision maker, you have 20 days to request a hearing, and the thing worth protecting is your insurance (SDIP), not points.

local.h: Boston details, verified against the MassDOT Registry of Motor Vehicles
bullets: Massachusetts civil motor vehicle citations are not heard by a city court. The Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) adjudicates them: you have 20 days from the citation to respond, either by paying the fine in full or by appealing and requesting a hearing.

Miss the 20 days and you lose the hearing plus pay late and release fees on top of the fine. If you do not then pay within 30 days of the RMV's default letter, your driver's licence or right to operate is suspended - this is the mechanism that catches most people out.

Ways to pay: online - but wait 10 days after you receive the citation before paying online, because the RMV needs time to receive and process it; by mail with a cheque or money order payable to MassDOT, citation and licence numbers written on it, to Citation Processing Center, P.O. Box 55890, Boston, MA 02205-5890 (never cash); or by phone at (857) 368-8000.

The hearing is where a ticket actually gets beaten or amended. You request a hearing on the ticket and it is heard by a clerk-magistrate, with a filing fee. If you are unhappy with the outcome you can appeal to the District Court, where a judge hears it fresh.

Watch the difference: a criminal traffic case - DUI, driving to endanger, leaving the scene - goes to the Boston Municipal Court or another District Court, not to the RMV. The civil citation process above does not apply to those.
Insurance is the real bill. A 'responsible' finding creates SDIP surcharge points that follow you for years, so the hearing is worth taking even when the fine itself is small.

cities.pay_label: NY DMV - plead to or pay a TVB ticket
cities.court_label: NY DMV - traffic tickets in New York State (TVB, hearings, payment plans)
cities.fine_note: TVB fines come from a statutory schedule for each violation, and a mandatory state surcharge is added on top of every fine. The amount you will owe for a guilty plea is shown before you submit it - the fine schedule and surcharge are what make a New York ticket more expensive than the posted number suggests.
cities.school_eligible: New York has no ticket-dismissal course. It does have the Point & Insurance Reduction Program (PIRP): completing an approved course reduces by 4 the number of points used to decide whether to suspend your licence, once in any 18-month period, and gives a 10% insurance discount for three years on the liability and collision parts of your premium. It does not remove the violation or conviction from your record.
cities.points_note: New York adds points per conviction and can suspend your licence at 11 points in 18 months. The DMV's point-reduction course shaves up to 4 points off that calculation but never removes the conviction itself.
cities.lawyer_cost: $300-$600 typical for a NYC TVB ticket (often a flat fee)
cities.tool_note: New York City tickets go to the DMV's TVB, not a local court. The record-protection tools are pleading not guilty and, later, the PIRP course (4 points off the suspension calculation).

local.h: New York City details, verified against the NY DMV Traffic Violations Bureau
bullets: If your ticket was issued in any of the five boroughs, it goes to the DMV's Traffic Violations Bureau (TVB) - not to a local court. Everywhere else in New York State it goes to a town, village or county court, which is a completely different process. The TVB handles all non-criminal traffic violation tickets in the city.

Two choices: plead guilty and pay the fine plus the mandatory surcharge (which puts points on your record), or plead not guilty and get a hearing. You can look up a full fine schedule before you decide what a guilty plea would actually cost you.

Hearings are now virtual, and if you are appearing without a lawyer you can file a Statement in Place of Personal Appearance (SIPOPA) instead of showing up. This is why so many New York tickets are resolved without anyone going to a building.
Lost the ticket? The DMV will let you print a substitute for any open TVB ticket online - you verify one ticket and can then print all of your open ones.

Points: 11 points in 18 months can suspend your licence. The Point & Insurance Reduction Program reduces the points used for that calculation by 4, once in any 18-month period, and earns a 10% insurance discount for three years - but it does not erase the violation from your record.
Paying it off: after your case is decided you may be eligible for a payment plan; the DMV's traffic ticket page explains how to apply and how to keep paying an existing plan.

cities.court_label: Pennsylvania UJS portal - case lookup and PAePay

local.h: Philadelphia details, checked against the City and the courts

Parking escalates fast: unpaid Philadelphia Parking Authority tickets lead to booting and towing, and you have to settle the balance in person to get the vehicle back.

local.h: Columbus details, checked against the Franklin County Clerk

cities.points_note: Ohio assesses points on conviction, and 12 points in two years triggers a 12-point suspension (a class-D suspension that typically runs six months). The BMV can act well before that, and points stay on your record for two years from the conviction.

local.h: Cleveland details, checked against the Clerk of Courts
bullets: Cleveland moving violations are handled by the Cleveland Municipal Court and its Waiver Bureau. The Clerk of Courts sits at 1200 Ontario Street, Cleveland, Ohio 44113.

Online: the Clerk's page links straight to the payment system - click through from the court's own site rather than searching, because third-party 'pay your ticket' sites charge extra and are not the court.
By mail: send a check or money order to Cleveland Municipal Court / Waiver Bureau / P.O. Box 99639 / Cleveland, Ohio 44199-0639.
In person: some offences require a court appearance. If you cannot complete the payment online, the court says to call 216-664-4790 or email clerkofcourts@cmcoh.org.
Parking is separate. Cleveland parking citations go through the Parking Violations Bureau (216-664-4744), which has its own payment site and its own contest process.
Ohio points land on your BMV record, and 12 points in two years triggers a 12-point suspension - typically six months. A BMV-approved remedial course earns a 2-point credit.

cities.court_label: 36th District Court, Detroit - court home page
cities.fine_note: Fines and court costs vary by violation. Check the court's current fine schedule, and treat the amount printed on your court notice as the real number.
cities.school_eligible: Michigan's real record saver is the Basic Driver Improvement Course (BDIC), run by the Secretary of State: an eligible driver who completes it avoids the points, and the ticket is not reported to insurance. You may only use it once, the State mails you a notice with a 60-day deadline to enrol, and you are not eligible if you already had more than 2 points when the ticket was issued, if the offence was criminal, if it happened in a commercial vehicle, if the ticket was issued outside Michigan, or if you hold a CDL.
cities.points_note: Michigan assesses points on conviction and keeps them for two years from the conviction date. 12 points in two years triggers a Secretary of State driver reexamination, which can end in a restriction, a suspension or a revocation.
cities.lawyer_cost: $300-$600 typical for a Detroit traffic citation
cities.tool_note: Michigan mails you the chance to avoid the points: if your ticket qualifies, the Secretary of State sends a letter and you have 60 days to enrol in the Basic Driver Improvement Course. Miss the letter and the points and the violation go to your insurer.

local.h: Detroit details, checked against the 36th District Court
bullets: Detroit traffic cases go to the 36th District Court at 421 Madison Street, Detroit, MI 48226 - one of the busiest courts in the country.
Online: the court runs its own online payment form. By phone: payments are taken 24 hours a day, in English or Spanish, on 1-855-798-1547.
Kiosks: the court operates payment kiosks across Metro Detroit, plus one right outside the building on Brush Street. Cashier's window: 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday.
By mail or drop box: put the citation number on a check or money order payable to 36th District Court. Never mail or deposit cash.
Cannot pay in full? The court runs an Online Collections Application for monthly payment plans over traffic tickets.

The record saver in Michigan is the Basic Driver Improvement Course (BDIC). Complete it and the ticket is not reported to your insurer, but you can only use it once, you must act inside the State's 60-day deadline, and you are out of luck if you already had more than 2 points, the offence was criminal, it happened in a commercial vehicle, the ticket came from outside Michigan, or you hold a CDL.

cities.court_label: Davidson County Circuit Court Clerk - Traffic Violation Bureau
cities.fine_note: Fines and court costs vary by violation. Check the court's current fine schedule, and treat the amount printed on your court notice as the real number.
cities.school_eligible: Tennessee does let a course help, in two different ways. A court-ordered traffic school can get a citation dismissed if the judge allows it, and separately the Department of Safety will remove up to 5 points from a speeding conviction if you complete an approved 4-hour driver education course. Course providers must send your certificate to the Department within 30 days, so ask the school who files it.
cities.points_note: Tennessee's Department of Safety runs a driver-improvement point system: 12 points in 12 months can bring a proposed suspension and a hearing. Points stay on your record for years, and it is the insurance effect that usually costs the most.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Davidson County's own office warns about ticket scams, so check the address bar: the only official payment site is the Clerk's paytraffic.nashville.gov, and the Traffic Violation Bureau is inside the county courthouse.

local.h: Nashville details, checked against the Clerk's own site
bullets: Nashville and Davidson County citations are handled by the Traffic Violation Bureau, part of the Davidson County Circuit Court Clerk's Office, at 408 2nd Avenue North, Suite 1160.
Pay online through paytraffic.nashville.gov - that is the Clerk's own payment site.

The Clerk's office publishes a public alert about outstanding-ticket scams. Genuine court business will not arrive as a text demanding immediate payment; if you get one, call the Bureau instead of clicking.
Court dockets for traffic and Metro citations are published by the Bureau, so you can check your own court date and outcome without going through a paid lookup service.
The Bureau also handles installment payment requests with a motion form - useful if the fine will not fit in one month.

Tennessee will remove up to 5 points from a speeding conviction if you complete an approved 4-hour driver education course, and a court-ordered traffic school can get the citation dismissed outright if the judge agrees. Course providers must file your certificate within 30 days.

cities.pay_label: Mecklenburg County payment information (NC Judicial Branch)
cities.court_label: NC eCourts Portal - look up and pay a citation
cities.fine_note: North Carolina fines plus court costs, and the costs are often larger than the fine. The court's own notice is the amount that counts.
cities.school_eligible: North Carolina does not use traffic school. The three standard moves are a plea to a lesser speed (generally 9 mph over or less, which avoids insurance points), a plea to Improper Equipment, and a Prayer for Judgment Continued (a PJC, where the court withholds judgment so no points post). The limits and the insurance treatment differ, so confirm what your court will accept.
cities.points_note: North Carolina runs two point systems at once, and the insurance one costs far more. Convictions add DMV points (12 points in three years can suspend your licence), while insurers use a separate scale where a single insurance point commonly raises premiums by around 30%.
cities.lawyer_cost: $200-$400 typical for a Charlotte speeding ticket
cities.tool_note: North Carolina is the one state where the insurance system punishes harder than the licence system. One insurance point is commonly a 30% premium increase, which is why a plea to 9 mph over or to Improper Equipment is worth asking about.

local.h: Charlotte details, checked against the NC Judicial Branch
bullets: Mecklenburg County citations are processed by the Clerk of Superior Court at the Mecklenburg County Courthouse. The mailing address for payments is PO Box 37971, Charlotte, NC 28237-7971.

By mail the Clerk takes a money order or certified check only - no cash and no personal cheques - payable to Mecklenburg County Clerk of Superior Court, and you should include a copy of the citation. Only pay by mail if your citation is marked as eligible.
In person at the Cashier's Office you can use cash, card, money order or certified check; card payments add a processing fee, and there is an ATM on Level 2.
Online, North Carolina moved to the statewide eCourts Portal. That is where you find the case, see whether it is payable, and pay it if it is.

The interesting move in North Carolina is not a course, it is the plea: 9 mph over or less avoids insurance points, Improper Equipment avoids them too, and a PJC (Prayer for Judgment Continued) has the court withhold judgment. Ask the clerk or a local attorney what your court will accept, because the limits are enforced.
DMV points and insurance points are different scales. 12 DMV points in three years can suspend your licence; a single insurance point can raise your premium by roughly 30%.

cities.points_note: Oregon does not use a point system. The DMV keeps your convictions on a driving record, and too many of them can put you into the Driver Improvement Program and cost you your licence, so the record still matters even though there are no points to count.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Oregon has no points to protect, but it does have a written-explanation trap on parking citations: sending in your explanation is a waiver of your right to a hearing.
