local.h: Portland details, checked against the court and the city
bullets: Traffic citations in Portland go to the Multnomah County Circuit Court, part of the Oregon Judicial Department. Parking citations issued by the city are dealt with through the City of Portland's parking process and the same circuit court's parking office.

Parking, by mail: use the yellow envelope, a cheque or money order payable to State of Oregon (never cash), and include the citation or case number plus the licence plate. The address is Multnomah County Circuit Court, Parking Citation Office, P.O. Box 78, Portland, OR 97207.
Parking, by phone: Visa or Mastercard, on 971-274-0590, pressing option 5. Online: the Oregon Judicial Department's ePay portal, which needs your county and citation details.

The trap: sending a written explanation instead of paying is treated as a waiver of your right to a court hearing and as consent to whatever judgment the judge makes on the papers. If you want to be heard, schedule the hearing instead.

You can usually view the violation photos online before deciding - you need the citation number (near the top, starting with HA), the citation date and the plate. Photos can take up to three days to appear.

If your car was towed or booted for unpaid parking citations you must pay the full balance in guaranteed funds at the Circuit Court Customer Service Area on the second floor - and the tow company adds its own fee before releasing the car.

cities.pay_label: Salt Lake City Justice Court - online payment centre
cities.court_label: Salt Lake City Justice Court - official page
cities.fine_note: Utah publishes a uniform fine schedule, and the Justice Court posts it. That schedule - not a third-party estimate - is what your violation costs.
cities.school_eligible: Utah courts usually offer two record-saving routes instead of a plain fine: Deferred Traffic Prosecution (you pay, stay clean for the deferral period, and the charge is dismissed) and traffic school. Both are court-by-court, so ask your justice court which it runs and whether you qualify.
cities.points_note: Utah's Driver License Division assigns points by violation - a red light is 50, following too closely is 60, reckless driving is 80, and speeding runs 35 to 75 - and more than 200 points in three years can suspend your privileges (the threshold is 70 for a driver under 21).
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Salt Lake City's Justice Court gives you three doors on the same page: pay the citation, request Deferred Traffic Prosecution, or request traffic school. Taking the right one is worth more than arguing about the fine.

local.h: Salt Lake City details, checked against the Justice Court
bullets: Salt Lake City citations go to the Salt Lake City Justice Court at the John L. Baxter Courthouse, 333 S 200 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84111.

Online: the court's own payment centre accepts a court case number, citation number or driver's licence number. Check the name on the case before you pay - the court warns about payments posted to the wrong case.
By phone: 801-535-6300, with phone hours 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday to Friday; the counter is open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
You can also schedule your arraignment and use MyCase to read your case before deciding anything - which is useful, because the court's options are not identical for every violation.
Utah's two record-saving routes are Deferred Traffic Prosecution (pay, stay clean for the deferral period, and the charge is dismissed) and traffic school. Both are offered case by case.

Points are computed by the Driver License Division: a red light is 50 points, following too closely 60, reckless driving 80, speeding 35 to 75, while more than 200 points in three years - or 70 for a driver under 21 - is what triggers a suspension.

cities.pay_label: Kansas City Municipal Court - fines, payments and sentences
cities.court_label: Missouri Case.net - look up your case
cities.fine_note: Kansas City publishes a payable-violations fine schedule and a separate court-costs table. Check your violation against the schedule before you pay, because payable and non-payable cases are treated completely differently.
cities.school_eligible: Missouri's route is the Driver Improvement Program, a state course aimed at stopping points from reaching your record and at reducing what is already there. Eligibility and the court's willingness vary, so confirm with the court or the Department of Revenue before you pay for it.
cities.points_note: Missouri's Department of Revenue sends you an advisory letter at 4 points in 12 months and suspends your driving privilege at 8 or more points in 18 months (30 days the first time, 60 the second, 90 after that). 12 points in 12 months means a one-year revocation. Points fall by a third for each clean year and reach zero after three.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: In Kansas City the first question is whether your case is payable at all. If the violation is on the court's payable fine schedule and you pay before the court date, you never go to court - if it is not, the judge decides the penalty.

local.h: Kansas City details, checked against the Municipal Court
bullets: Kansas City citations go to the Kansas City Municipal Court, 511 E. 11th Street, Kansas City, MO 64106.
Online, payment runs through Missouri Case.net. Search by case number, or by name using Jackson County - 16th Judicial Circuit and then Kansas City Municipal in the court dropdown.

The rule that matters: if the case is before the court date printed on your ticket and the violation is on the court's payable fine schedule, you can pay without appearing. On non-payable cases the judge sets the penalty if you plead guilty or are found guilty.
By mail: cheque or money order payable to Municipal Court, with your name and the ticket or payment-plan number. No cash by mail.
In person: the Violations Bureau takes card, cash, cheque or money order. The lobby kiosk takes debit or credit cards, and the drop box takes cheque or money order only.
Older tickets may live in a different system: cases from before 6 November 2023 are in the legacy system, which is why a search can come back empty. Court help: 816-513-2700 or court@kcmo.org.
Missouri points come from the Department of Revenue: a warning at 4 points in 12 months, suspension at 8 or more points in 18 months, and revocation at 12 points in 12 months.

cities.pay_label: Minnesota Judicial Branch - pay a ticket
cities.court_label: Hennepin County Violations Bureau & Hearing Office
cities.fine_note: Minnesota publishes the fine for each violation, and the court adds a surcharge. The notice from the court is the amount that counts.
cities.school_eligible: Minnesota has no statewide course that removes a ticket. Many district courts do run a violations bureau hearing-officer route where you can ask for a reduction without a trial, and that is usually the cheapest thing to try.
cities.points_note: Minnesota has no point system at all. What does bite is insurance, plus the habitual-violator law: four traffic convictions in one year, or five in two years, brings a 30-day suspension (90 days for another conviction inside those windows). Minor speeding - no more than 10 over in a 55, or 5 over in a 60 - is not even recorded on your DPS driving record.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Minnesota has no points, so the argument for hiring anyone is weaker than in most states. The violations bureau hearing-officer route is the cheap first move.

local.h: Minneapolis details, checked against the Minnesota Judicial Branch
bullets: Minneapolis citations are handled by the Hennepin County District Court and its Violations Bureau & Hearing Office. The Records Center is at 300 South 6th Street, #SK-0260, Minneapolis, MN 55487-0332.
Pay online through the Minnesota Judicial Branch's pay-a-ticket service, in person with cash, card or money order, or by mail with a cheque or money order payable to Hennepin County District Court.
Minnesota has no point system. That is worth knowing before you spend money to 'keep points off' - there are none to keep off.
What does exist is the habitual violator law: four convictions in one year, or five in two years, brings a 30-day suspension - and 90 days for another conviction inside either window.
Minor speeding is not even recorded: no more than 10 mph over in a 55, or 5 over in a 60, is left off your DPS driving record.
The practical lever is the hearing officer, not a course. Ask the Violations Bureau whether your case can be heard that way - it is faster and cheaper than a trial.

cities.pay_label: Marion County Traffic Division (City of Indianapolis)
cities.court_label: Indiana MyCase - look up and manage your case
cities.fine_note: Indiana fines come with court costs, and the traffic division collects both. Check the amount on the citation or in MyCase before you pay.
cities.school_eligible: Indiana's BMV-approved defensive driving / driver safety programmes can reduce points and are often accepted by courts in place of a conviction. Which course and whether it helps is decided by the court and the BMV, so ask before you enrol.
cities.points_note: Indiana assesses points through the BMV: 14 to 18 points brings a warning letter, 20 points a one-month suspension, and it escalates from there (Indiana Administrative Code, 140 IAC 1). Reckless driving and major offences carry their own penalties.
cities.lawyer_cost: $250-$500 typical for a simple moving violation
cities.tool_note: Indianapolis traffic cases run through the Marion County Traffic Division, and you can read the whole case in MyCase before you decide anything. The due date on an Indiana ticket is short - treat the date printed on the citation as the deadline, not the date you got around to reading it.
verify: the exact due date printed on your citation

local.h: Indianapolis details, checked against the city and the state courts
bullets: Indianapolis citations are handled by the Marion County Traffic Division, which processes infractions, moving violations and traffic misdemeanours for the city.

In person: the main location is the Community Justice Campus, 675 Justice Way. There is also a counter in Room W122, City-County Building, 200 E. Washington Street. Both are open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and both take cash and cards.

By mail: a money order or cashier's cheque to Marion County Traffic Division, 200 E. Washington Street, Indianapolis, IN 46204, with a copy of the ticket. Do not mail cash, and do not assume a personal cheque will be accepted for every ticket type.
Look the case up in MyCase first. Indiana's state case system shows the charges, the hearing dates and the amount owed, and it is free.
The due date on an Indiana citation is 60 days from the day you received it. Miss it and the case can be escalated to a failure to appear, which adds costs and can affect your licence.

Indiana assesses points through the BMV: 14 to 18 points brings a warning letter and 20 points a one-month suspension, escalating from there. A BMV-approved defensive-driving course can reduce points, and courts often accept one instead of a conviction - ask before you enrol.
